rationale: C01 supplies the closest reusable letter template: both letters congratulate an addressee on the successful completion of a program, extend praise through the addressee to everyone who cooperated, and conclude that the participants may take pride in the accomplishment. C07 and C19 more closely match the Red Cross and humanitarian subject matter, with C07 also paralleling the child’s nondiscrimination language, but they are campaign memoranda with substantially different operative purposes and structures.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I wish to express to you and through you to every member of your organization who participated in the successful accomplishment of this undertaking my sincere appreciation, as well as my congratulations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I greatly appreciate your report on the success of the Veterans Administration program... You and all who cooperated with you in this program are to be highly commended.
shared_material.explanation: Both use an appreciation-and-congratulation formula addressed to a program leader and explicitly extend the commendation to all participants.

shared_material.child_excerpt: They can be proud of their work.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In your accomplishment, Americans everywhere can take a great and justifiable pride.
shared_material.explanation: The letters close their substantive praise with the same pride-in-accomplishment motif.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The relief program... is now practically completed... I know that the success of the program is in a large measure due to the untiring efforts of the members of your organization.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I greatly appreciate your report on the success of the Veterans Administration program... In making the success of your program possible...
shared_material.explanation: Both organize the message around a successfully accomplished program and credit those whose cooperation made that success possible.
